# Slide Blueprint: One Effective Exam Prep Strategy

**Generated by:** Skill 04 — Slides Generation
**Workshop slug:** exam_prep_strategy
**Total slides:** 6
**Deck tone:** Direct, honest, slightly provocative — like a good piece of advice from a senior student
**Color palette:** Deep navy (#1A2744) + clean white (#FFFFFF) + energetic amber (#F5A623)
**Font suggestion:** Headings: Inter Bold / Body: Inter Regular

---

## Visual System

The deck uses a deep navy base with white type and amber accents — a palette that feels focused and serious without being corporate. Every slide has one dominant element and generous whitespace. The visual language is deliberately sparse: slides are cue cards for the facilitator, not content delivery surfaces. No decorative elements, no gradients, no stock photography of people studying.

---

## Slides

---

### Slide 01 — Arrival / Title Card
**Phase:** A — Arrival
**Layout:** Title card
**Content:**
- Title: **The Most Effective Study Technique You're Probably Not Using**
- Subtitle: *By the end of this session, you'll have already used it.*
- Presenter: [Name] · [Date/Context]

**Speaker cue:** Read the subtitle aloud. Let the implied promise ("you'll have already done it") land for a moment, then move straight into the reactivation question.

**Design Prompt:**
> Full-bleed deep navy background (#1A2744). Title centered in large white Inter Bold — maximum 3 lines. Subtitle in medium Inter Regular, off-white (#E8E8E8), below with a small gap. Presenter name/date very small at bottom. No images, no icons, no decorative elements. The feeling is confident and slightly provocative — like a good opening line that makes you sit up. Avoid gradients, stock images, and anything decorative.

---

### Slide 02 — Reactivating Question
**Phase:** R — Reactivating
**Layout:** Quote card
**Content:**
- Large text: **"You studied hard. You still blanked on the exam. 🖐 Raise your hand."**
- Small label: *Think about the last time it happened.*

**Speaker cue:** Read the question aloud and then wait silently. Let the hands go up before you say anything. This pause is important — don't rush it.

**Design Prompt:**
> Same navy base as Slide 01. The question fills 65–70% of the slide in large Inter Bold white type. The "🖐 Raise your hand." line can be slightly smaller or in amber for emphasis. Small italic label at the bottom in muted off-white. No images. The pause this slide creates is the point — the layout should feel open and expectant, not cluttered.

---

### Slide 03 — Informing: The Illusion of Knowing
**Phase:** I — Informing
**Layout:** Two-column
**Content:**
- Headline: **Familiar ≠ Remembered**
- Left column: Two short lines — *"Re-reading: feels like learning."* / *"Exam: the feeling vanishes."*
- Right column: Simple diagram — two circles: one labelled "RECOGNITION" (seeing it again), one labelled "RECALL" (retrieving without prompts), with an arrow showing the gap between them

**Speaker cue:** This slide is a visual anchor while you deliver the push-up analogy verbally. Don't read the slide — use it as a backdrop to the spoken explanation.

**Design Prompt:**
> Navy background. Headline in large amber Inter Bold at the top. Left column in white Inter Regular — short, punchy phrases only, wide line spacing. Right column: a clean, minimal two-circle diagram in white with amber labels — "RECOGNITION" and "RECALL" — with an arrow or gap between them labeled "← the exam gap". The diagram should feel like something drawn on a whiteboard, not a polished infographic. No shadows, no gradients. Whitespace is the design.

---

### Slide 04 — Informing: What Retrieval Practice Looks Like
**Phase:** I — Informing (continued)
**Layout:** Full-image with overlay
**Content:**
- Single large visual: blank sheet of paper with a pen, seen from above — minimalist
- Overlay text (top): **Close your notes.**
- Overlay text (bottom): **Write what you remember.**
- Small amber badge: *Do the reps.*

**Speaker cue:** Advance to this slide when you move from "why re-reading fails" to "here's what to do instead." The visual makes the method concrete and non-technical. Say the two overlay lines aloud as you advance.

**Design Prompt:**
> This slide breaks from the navy base — use a very light warm grey or off-white background to signal a shift in tone from explaining to showing. Clean overhead photograph (or flat illustration) of a blank white sheet of paper and a simple pen — nothing else. Overlay text in navy Inter Bold, top and bottom of the image, with generous margins. Small amber rounded badge in the lower right corner with "Do the reps." in white. The feeling is clean, practical, and immediate.

---

### Slide 05 — Verarbeitung Task
**Phase:** V — Verarbeitung
**Layout:** Instruction card
**Content:**
- Title: **Your turn.**
- Numbered steps:
  1. Pick one topic you're studying right now.
  2. Close your notes. No phone.
  3. Write everything you remember. Don't look.
- Timer badge: **2 minutes ⏱**

**Speaker cue:** Read the three steps aloud slowly and clearly before starting the timer. Leave this slide visible the entire time participants are working. Start a visible timer immediately after saying "Go."

**Design Prompt:**
> Return to the navy base. Title "Your turn." in large amber Inter Bold at the top — this signals a phase change to active mode. Numbered list in large white Inter Regular, widely spaced — one step per visual breath. Timer badge in amber, bottom-right corner, large and legible: "2 min ⏱". The slide should feel like a clear, unambiguous instruction card. No decoration. The steps should be readable from the back of the room.

---

### Slide 06 — Assessing Question
**Phase:** A — Assessing
**Layout:** Takeaway card
**Content:**
- Large text: **"Who found at least one gap — something you thought you knew but couldn't recall? 🖐"**

**Speaker cue:** Ask the question aloud, let the hands go up, then deliver the closing line verbally: "That discomfort is the learning. Use your gaps. That's retrieval practice." Do not read the closing line from a slide.

**Design Prompt:**
> Navy base, slightly warmer than the opening slides — consider a very subtle shift toward a dark blue-teal (#1A3044) to signal the loop is closing. The question fills the slide in large white Inter Bold. The 🖐 emoji can be in amber for warmth. No other elements. The feeling is calm and conclusive — like the last line of a good lesson.

---

## Design System Summary

**Fonts:** Inter Bold (headings, callouts, emphasis) / Inter Regular (body, labels)
**Colors:**
- Primary background: Deep navy #1A2744
- Primary text: White #FFFFFF
- Accent / emphasis: Amber #F5A623
- Slide 04 background: Off-white / warm grey #F4F2EE
- Supporting text: Off-white #E8E8E8

**Image style:** Flat, clean, high-contrast — or none at all. One diagram (Slide 03), one minimal photograph/illustration (Slide 04). No stock photography of people.

**Transitions:** Cut only. No animations, no builds, no reveals. The content is the animation.

**Slide ratio:** 16:9
